- Module boundaries and state handling (multi-tenant state isolation)
- Network hardening (VLANs, route tables, flow logs, ACLs)
- CI gating (terraform plan gating, policy checks)
- Rollback/playbook for failed upgrades (DB migration rollback, agent reverts)

I attached the current artifacts (tf modules, helm chart values, and a draft rollback playbook). There's a PR with the full diffs: https://github.com/edgegrid/priv-deploy/pull/42. Please treat the repo as sensitive; we'll grant staging access for hands-on checks.

Can your team complete an initial pass by EOD May 18? If not, propose an alternate date. We also want a short runbook section explicitly calling out pre-deploy smoke tests and post-deploy validation steps.

Thanks,
Siddharth Rao
Head of Infra, EdgeGrid

I'll pick up the Terraform/CI side. Early notes after a quick scan of the PR:
- There are a couple of global state references in module root that could cause collisions if multiple environments share the same backend. Recommend per-environment prefixes and explicit workspace handling.
- Some sensitive variables (db_password, s3_token) are plain strings in the example tfvars; we should enforce usage of a secrets manager provider and add a policy check (terraform-validate-policy) in CI.
- Add a terraform plan artifact upload step to CI and a required approver on the PR for any changes to core networking modules.

I'll open two PRs against EdgeGrid: one that adds an automated plan/scan job in the pipeline and one with a proposed variable/secrets layout. I'll also sketch the pre/post-deploy smoke tests (svc ping, agent registration check, sample inference request).

Short timeline: initial CI PR by May 17 (end of day PT), tf variable hardening PR by May 18.

- Dev

Couple of deeper network/runtime items I want to call out for the review and the runbook:

- Subnet and AZ mapping: For on-prem / VPC-hybrid, ensure deterministic subnet naming and explicit CIDR boundaries. Prefer explicit route tables per subnet to avoid accidental cross-talk.
- BGP / routing: If you rely on BGP peerings for on-prem fabric, include a clear step to drain and advertise withdrawn routes before any disruptive change.
- Host network hardening: Recommend host-level firewall baseline (ufw/iptables) with a policy document in the repo and Ansible roles that enforce it.
- K8s considerations: Force kube-proxy in ipvs mode, set kubelet eviction thresholds, and include Helm hooks for pre-upgrade backups of PVs. Charts should include tolerations and probe timeouts tuned for on-prem latency.
- Rollback mechanics: Do not rely on helm rollback alone for DB schema changes. For any change that touches DB migrations, include an explicit backward-compatible migration pattern + a documented manual rollback that restores DB snapshot and reconciles schema.
- CI: Add a terratest job for core networking modules (vpc, subnets, route tables) against a lightweight emulator or a staging environment to catch drift early.

I'll add these as comments in the PR and prepare a short network hardening checklist for the runbook. We also need access to the staging BGP config to run a dry-run.

- Markus
